title: Intentional Sprint Compass: weekly journal & KPI experiments
content:
Purpose: quick, usable scratchpad to track weekly intentions, micro-KPIs, and lightweight experiments for the quarter. Not polished — honest notes, friction points, and small bets. Use this to seed the weekly retro and to transfer outcomes into the formal OKR doc when something sticks.

Quarter-level Northstar (Q4 personal): increase reliable focus blocks and ship three measurable productivity experiments that reduce context-switching cost by >=15%.

Key personal KPIs (measured weekly/monthly):
- Deep focus hours/week (goal: 12) — calendar blocks of 90+ minutes where no meetings + no Slack.
- Flow tasks completed per week (goal: 5) — tasks that require uninterrupted thought (design, eval results, writeups).
- Weekly review completion (goal: 100%) — short 20m review on Friday, add one improvement.
- Task switch latency (experiment metric): median time between context switch start and back-in-flow (baseline: ~18m).

Weekly check template (use each Monday):
1) 3 priorities this week (explicit outcomes, not activities).
2) Availability windows (blocked off deep work times).
3) Experiment to run (one small change to measure).
4) Anticipated blockers and mitigation.

Recent entries — quick logs:
2026-02-24 (Mon)
- Priorities: finish small-run evaluation harness; write follow-up notes for Maya; prototype a tiny calendar auto-blocker.
- Availability: 09:30-11:00, 14:00-16:00 deep blocks.
- Experiment: Silent mornings — no Slack/Email until 11:00. Hypothesis: >2 extra deep-focus hours.
- Notes: felt more present in morning. Interrupted at 10:40 for infra incident (took ~22m to return to flow).

2026-02-26 (Wed)
- Retro quick: Silent mornings gave +1.5h measurable deep time but I still frag at 10:40. Pattern: early interruptions typically from on-call rotation or PR pings.
- Tactic: add a 10m triage slot at 10:30 instead of ad-hoc checks.

2026-02-27 (Thu)
- Data point: Flow tasks completed = 4 (within goal). Deep hours = 10. Action: push for one uninterrupted 3-hour block next week.

Mini-experiments log (what I ran, what I learned):
- Silent mornings (2 weeks) — result: +1.2 average deep hours/week, but susceptible to single high-eyeball interrupts. Tradeoff: delayed async responses to team.
- 10m triage slot (trial) — reduced median switch latency from ~18m to ~12m when used; success if kept disciplined.
- Meeting triage map (visual) — mapped recurring meetings that pull me out of flow; identified one weekly sync that can be async.

Unresolved questions / Notes to self:
- Is there a way to route non-urgent infra pings to a buffer? (follow up with Arjun re on-call policy RDW-2345).
- How to measure context-switch cost more robustly without heavy instrumentation? Short idea: use timestamped task start markers in a tiny spreadsheet and capture interruption reason — do for 2 weeks.

Action items for next retro (assign to me unless noted):
- Convert winning experiment (10m triage slot) into a persistent habit for 3 weeks and re-measure.
- Draft a short Slack post describing my new expected response window to set team expectations (tag: @oncall to avoid surprises).
- Move one weekly sync to an async doc; propose at Tuesday 1:1 with Maya.

Retrospective notes (meta):
- What worked: small bounded changes (10m slots, silent mornings) are easier to adopt than sweeping calendar surgery.
- What didn't: vague promises to 'focus more' — need measurable definition (deep hours, flow tasks).
- Social friction: being less responsive creates small anxiety; need explicit framing to team so it doesn't create upstream friction.

Quick templates to copy into weekly reviews: 
- Week of DATE: deep hours=X, flow tasks=Y, key wins=[...], blockers=[...], experiment outcome=[success/mixed/fail], next week hypothesis=[...].

Links and references in flight: 
- Playbook draft: conf:team-personal-playbook-42 (seed ideas for habit engineering).
- Notes-to-convert: GitHub PR with lightweight time-tracking tool: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/pull/78
- Jira followups: RDW-2345 (on-call triage policy).

Final quick thought: treat this doc as a 10-minute end-of-week ritual — update one line, keep momentum. If an experiment crosses the threshold (>15% improvement) convert to a formal tracked OKR and bring data to the team retro.

(End — scratchpad; prune when turning into official OKR doc.)
